clue.text: Liberal entering contest will be made to follow through

indicators.note: entering tells us the Liberal letter goes into the middle of the contest word

parts.note: to contest is to compete

explanation.surface: A Liberal candidate joining a race will be forced to see it through to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete a task is to follow it through to its finish; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Botheration! 'e comes in to attract attention

indicators.note: comes in says the dropped-h letter sits inside the attention-getting sound

parts.note: psst or pst is the hissing noise made to attract someone's attention
taken as written, the dropped-aitch form of he

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in irritation as a man barges in trying to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance or source of annoyance is a botheration, a synonym in its noun sense.

clue.text: Contrary girl claims south's hot and squelchy

indicators.note: claims means takes in, so the girl's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Mary, Mary, quite contrary is the English nursery rhyme heroine
S is the abbreviation for south
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An awkward young woman insists the southern ground is hot and soggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' is a traditional English nursery rhyme, so a contrary girl is MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that squelches underfoot is wet and boggy, like a marsh.

clue.text: Kind of popular music prods smallest of the family to get up again

indicators.note: prods means pokes into, so the music genre is pushed inside the small animal

parts.note: the runt is the smallest animal in a litter
emo is a genre of emotional rock music

explanation.surface: A style of pop music nudges the tiniest member of the family into rising once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To remount is to climb back on, as on a horse, so to get up again.

clue.text: A recent union member?

parts.note: union here is a marriage rather than a trade union, and a recent member of one is someone just married

explanation.definitionFit: Someone only just married has lately joined a marital union, which the question mark signals.

clue.text: Study Kipling's poem about Italian poet's bosom pal

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the poem's title is written backwards

parts.note: If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem
Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: Examining a Kipling poem about Dante's closest companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidante is a trusted close friend to whom secrets are told, a bosom pal.

clue.text: Asthmatic American's last letter returned in the form of a question

indicators.note: in places the turned letter name inside the question word

parts.note: why is a question word

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letter's name is read from its end

parts.note: Americans call the last letter of the alphabet zee

explanation.surface: An American asks about the final letter while struggling for breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asthmatic breathes with a whistling rasp, so is short of breath in that way.

clue.text: Old chap with passion for news reporting

parts.note: cove is old slang for a chap or fellow
rage is a passion or fury

explanation.surface: An elderly man has a fervour for journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: The coverage of a story is the extent to which the press reports it.

clue.text: Time in reverse is hard to deal with

indicators.note: in reverse says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to cope is to deal with something

explanation.surface: Time running backwards is a difficult thing to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of time, an era.

clue.text: Notice a bit of acne

definitions.meaning: to notice something is to see or catch sight of it
a single pimple on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to notice; a spot is also a pimple, one bit of acne.

clue.text: Given the slip for aspiring to be a self-helper

definitions.text: Given the slip for aspiring to be a self-helper

parts.words: Given the slip for aspiring to be a self-helper
parts.note: a self-helper here is one who helps himself to goods in a store, and giving the slip means evading staff

explanation.definitionFit: A thief in a shop helps himself to goods without paying, a mocking take on self-help.

clue.text: In France water temperature gets by without having a particular quality

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the two letters of by wrap the rest

parts.note: eau is French for water

explanation.surface: French water at a certain warmth gets by lacking any special characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty is a quality, the one of being pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Recut county suit, showing a slick style

indicators.note: recut means cut again into new shapes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor recuts a country gent's suit to give it a sleek look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recut' rearranges COUNTY SUIT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuosity is an oily, smooth manner, a slick and ingratiating style.

clue.text: A don's way strange for these times

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the s included

explanation.surface: An academic's manner seems odd in the modern age.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means at the present time, in these times.

clue.text: Little about student clubs, a short time back, could be acceptable

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the small word goes round the other letters

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
L is the learner, a student driver's plate
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: back means the short time is written in reverse

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: A small number of student societies, recently returned, might be welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something welcome is gladly received, so acceptable.

clue.text: Not very bright about estates forming part of the UK

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for dull is written backwards

parts.note: dim means not very bright
lands are estates of property

explanation.surface: Dull-witted people around landed properties that make up a region of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MIDLANDS is the central region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midlands is the central region of England, so part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Eccentricity of old clergyman seen by Scottish lake

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a clergyman
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A peculiar old vicar is spotted beside Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddness is strangeness, so a synonym for eccentricity.

clue.text: Tues: earn enough to afford wine

indicators.note: the letters are spent and reworked into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: On Tuesday you make enough money to buy a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enough to afford' rearranges TUES EARN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Quietly start again to take liberties

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
to resume is to start again

explanation.surface: Begin once more, softly, to overstep the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to behave too boldly, overstepping what is proper.

clue.text: Lose one's cool with girl subordinate

parts.note: Flo is a girl's name
under means lower in rank, subordinate

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper with a girl who works under them.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to become confused and struggle, losing composure.

clue.text: Got to know books, originally Shakespearean

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the Shakespeare piece goes first

parts.note: King Lear is a Shakespearean tragedy
NT, New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A scholar became familiar with books that were first written by Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Learnt is the past tense of learn, so got to know.

clue.text: Plump little flier with a bit of a headache — rubbish!

indicators.note: a bit of means part of, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A chubby kid who flies about gives one a slight headache, nonsense!
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a chubby winged child in art, so a plump little flier.

clue.text: Subtle service to replace one in city

indicators.note: to replace means one letter is swapped for something else

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
RAF, the Royal Air Force, is an armed service

explanation.surface: A subtle armed service replaces one person in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty means cunning, subtle in a sly way.

clue.text: Mum arranged rash delivery of ales to old prison

parts.note: ma is mum

indicators.note: arranged means set in order anew, so these letters are shuffled
delivery means sending round, so the letters of ales are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother organised an impulsive drinks drop to an ancient jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes RSHA from RASH, and 'delivery of' makes LSEA from ALES. The Marshalsea was a notorious London debtors' prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marshalsea was a historic debtors' prison in Southwark, London.

clue.text: Almost never returned to flat

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the shortened word is read backwards
almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nearly never came back to the apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the R from NEVER to give NEVE; 'returned' turns it into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level and smooth, flat.

clue.text: Leaders to end up running off with the money

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The bosses end up running away with the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency of much of Europe, so money.

clue.text: Marked absence of favourite toy

parts.note: no expresses a lack, the absence of something
ted is a teddy bear, a child's favourite toy

explanation.surface: A child's best-loved plaything was noticed missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means observed or marked down.

clue.text: Test soldiers in good way to travel

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Testing troops in a sound means of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly British roadworthiness test that cars must pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Motoring is travelling by car, a way to travel.
